gate: the candidate may not introduce a decision the baseline never produced, on any case of the frozen turn corpus. A variant that invents one decision is rejected however much it saves. Cases that are nondeterministic inside a single arm are reported rather than hidden, because a set comparison alone would overstate the gate.
method: the real sidecar per variant, whole sessions alternated in ABBA order, the same 12-case corpus twice per session. The candidate removes the two fields from the schema and BAXY fills them back in from mode and effect_operations, so everything downstream sees the identical decision shape.

verdict.status: REJECTED. Not promoted; production is unchanged.
verdict.gate: FAILED. no_new_decisions = false, and every other metric moved the wrong way.

measured.prompt_ms_p50: 369.5 -> 420.9 (prefill got WORSE, which was the whole point of the change)

verdict.why: moving the candidate catalog into the system turn puts it inside the prefix, so any change of shortlist now invalidates the ~554 tokens of system prompt that were being cached before. The shortlist comes from planner_catalog.shortlist(objective, ...) and changes often across this corpus, so the trade lost more cache than it won.
verdict.what_this_settles: the catalog cannot be prefix-cached by reordering. The earlier conclusion that this is inherent to the per-turn shortlist design was correct, and the later doubt about it was wrong. Caching it would require making the shortlist itself stable, which is a retrieval-design change and not a prompt change.
